bloques.titulo: Contrast: als versus wenn in the past
texto: **Als** = once in the past: **Als ich klein war, lernte ich Schwimmen** (when I was little I learned swimming). **Wenn / Immer wenn** = repetition in the past: **Immer wenn die Sonne schien, gingen wir an den Strand** (whenever the sun shone, we went to the beach).

Like «als», «wenn» is a subordinate conjunction and places the conjugated verb at the end: **Wenn wir früher frei hatten, fuhren wir ans Meer**. In the main sentence verbo- subject: **fuhren wir** is produced.

filas: Als ich in Wien ankam, regnete es.
Wenn wir frei hatten, fuhren wir ans Meer.
Immer wenn er Zeit hatte, las er ein Buch.
Jedes Mal wenn ich ihn sah, sprach er mit mir.

frases.de: Was habt ihr früher im Sommer gemacht?
frases.en: What were you doing before in summer?

frases.de: Wenn wir frei hatten, fuhren wir immer ans Meer.
frases.es: Cuando teníamos tiempo libre, íbamos siempre al mar.
frases.en: When we had free time, we were always going to the sea.

frases.de: Und seid ihr oft im Meer geschwommen?
frases.es: ¿Y nadabais a menudo en el mar?
frases.en: And did you often swim in the sea?

frases.de: Ja, immer wenn die Sonne schien, gingen wir an den Strand.
frases.es: Sí, siempre que brillaba el sol, íbamos a la playa.
frases.en: Yeah, as long as the sun was shining, we were going to the beach.

bloques.pregunta: What connector is used for regular and repeated actions in the past?

opciones.explicacion: «Wenn» expresses repetition («every time / whenever») both in the present and in the past.
«Als» is reserved exclusively for unique facts in the past.

bloques.pregunta: What's the difference between «Als ich krank war» and «Wenn ich krank war»?

opciones.texto: «Als» refers to a specific occasion and «wenn» to several occasions
opciones.explicacion: «Als» marks a punctual episode; «wenn» indicates that it occurred repeatedly («every time I got sick»).

opciones.texto: «Als» is used for the future and «wenn» for the past
opciones.explicacion: Both sentences are in the past, but «als» is punctual and «wenn» is repetitive.
In German the distinction between a single and a recurrent fact is mandatory.

bloques.frase: Immer ___ die Sonne schien, gingen wir im Park spazieren.

opciones.explicacion: «Immer wenn» introduces repetition («every time the sun shone»).
«Als» is not combined with «immer» for past repetitions.

bloques.frase: Wenn wir früher frei hatten, ___ wir jedes Wochenende ans Meer.

opciones.explicacion: Investment in the main sentence: verb in second position (fuhren wir).
«gefahren» is the participle and would require «sind» auxiliary.

bloques.frase: Wenn wir früher frei hatten, fuhren wir ans Meer.

opciones.texto: When we had free time, we went to the sea.
opciones.explicacion: wenn = when (sometimes repeated); frei hatten = we had free; fuhren = we were in vehicle.

opciones.texto: When we went to the sea for the one time, we had bad time.
opciones.explicacion: The prayer with «wenn» describes a usual custom.

opciones.texto: Since we didn't have any money, we stayed home.
opciones.explicacion: It completely disrupts the meaning of the phrase.

bloques.frase: Immer wenn mein Freund mich besuchte, ___ wir lange zusammen.
Wenn wir frei hatten fuhren wir ans Meer
bloques.traduccion: When we had free we went to the sea
bloques.explicacion: wenn places the verb at the end of the subordinate.

intro: When we want to express a repeated or usual action in the past («every time / whenever»), German does not use «als», but «wenn», usually reinforced by «immer wenn» or «jedes Mal wenn».
